assumptions: Onset is assumed to be 13:49, based on the first minute in which the flag logged a mixed on/off evaluation split and the first ZeroDivisionError appeared. The flag provider records an admin toggle at 13:54:08, five minutes later; the discrepancy was not explained, and we assume the earlier change was a percentage ramp that was not recorded as a discrete event.

The flag revert issued at 13:54:33 is assumed not to have taken effect. It was not confirmed at the provider; the only evidence is that the service kept logging the flag as 'on' with the same error afterwards. An alternative reading - that the revert applied but a stale cache, pinned config, or already-live code kept the faulty path reachable - was not ruled out.
Recovery was judged against a 180-second observation window after the revert. If the flag change needed longer than that to propagate, the action may have been marked refuted prematurely.

No deploy or release events appear in the change history for the days preceding the incident, so the defect is assumed to be latent in already-running code that the flag merely exposed, rather than newly shipped. This rests on the change log being complete.
The pre-incident baseline of low-level account-page failures was a separate, ongoing UpstreamTimeout condition, assumed unrelated to this incident and not investigated.
The incident end timestamp reflects escalation to a human, not verified recovery; errors were still present in the last logs read. The impact duration is therefore a lower bound.
The draft pull request is an untested proposal. It has not been reviewed, merged, or confirmed to fix the division fault.
input.executive_summary: Starting shortly before the alert fired on the afternoon of 17 September, a large share of requests to customer account pages failed with an error instead of rendering. The trigger was a newly switched-on feature that rolled out to most traffic, exposing a bug in the code it turned on. Only the account page was affected; the rest of the shop continued to serve normally, and no data was lost or corrupted. The automated responder attempted the obvious fix — turning the new feature back off — but the change did not take hold and the failures continued, so the responder stopped making further changes, opened a draft code fix for the underlying bug, and escalated to a human on-call engineer. The alert was open for roughly five and a half minutes; account-page failures were still being logged at the moment of handoff, so the end of the alert should not be read as the end of customer impact.
input.root_cause: A percentage rollout of the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop began evaluating "on" for most traffic during the 13:49 minute, and the code path it enables performs an unguarded division in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32`, so every account-page request that took the enabled path raised `ZeroDivisionError`. Logs show the flag still evaluating "on" and the same stack signature through 13:58 despite an automated flag revert at 13:54:33, so the failing path remained reachable for the whole window rather than being cleared by the revert.
